executiveSummary: GM1719's generated 2025 code, Drimmelen name, Noord-Brabant province, Midden- en West-Brabant safety-region assignment, 28,295-person control total, 38 neighbourhoods, seven BAG places and fifteen settlement labels are coherent. All ten canonical exercises execute deterministically at T+0/6/12/24/48/72 across power, water, drainage, gas, telecom, mobility, facilities and supply; exact-zero input, finite bounds, reconciliation, causal-ledger closure and layer invariance pass. Release remains correction-required. Official evidence places Drimmelen on the Amer/Benedenrivieren system behind primary defences, includes an outer-dike harbour development, identifies Biesbosch nature-fire conditions and publishes rain, heat, water-control and service-provider context. None of those mechanisms drives the local result. The generic river preset instead holds normalized inundation stress at 2.145597 through T+72, reports 7,214 affected people-equivalent and 896,140.193 attributable person-hours, and leaves drainage at 44.587% without a selected water boundary, defence/breach state, connected footprint, arrival or recession. Pluvial, river, coastal, heat and wildfire share the same complete neighbourhood order; a controlled fire inside the official Rupsenhoek/Sluishoek woodland still ranks its containing neighbourhood second. All eight lifelines reuse the same five NWB roads, while 164 public water objects, external acute care, 42 transit stops and provider areas do not establish topology, live capacity, backup or restoration. Public integrations can improve context and selected scenarios, but unavailable or security-sensitive operational infrastructure must remain Unknown or transparently synthetic rather than being implied by precise percentages.

evidenceSources.title: Kerncijfers wijken en buurten 2025, table 86165NED, OData API
supports: The fresh official GM1719 row gives Drimmelen, 28,295 residents, density 298 per square kilometre, 6,873 residents aged 65+, 3,849 one-person households and 12,445 households.

The 38 generated neighbourhood source rows sum exactly to 28,295 residents, 12,440 households and 6,870 residents aged 65+; the small household and age-control differences are consistent with CBS small-area rounding and suppression rather than model corrections.

The OData service is machine-readable under CC BY 4.0. CBS labels the 2025 table as receiving quarterly additions; randomized rounding, suppression and incomplete variables remain source semantics, not zero.
Simulation role is official demographic/context and allocation denominator only. Registered residence is not incident-time presence, mobility, evacuation demand or individual vulnerability.

evidenceSources.title: CBS Gebiedsindelingen 2025 non-generalized geometry and national settlement/transport reference APIs
evidenceSources.edition: 2025 boundary; current generated BAG, BRT, NWB, ProRail and GTFS reference editions
supports: Fresh full-resolution GM1719 geometry has one MultiPolygon component, one ring and 1,178 positions with bbox [4.645136584918031, 51.628862562742405, 4.853126169876171, 51.76656830368469]. The generated overview preserves that topology with 87 positions and contains centre [4.749560515173187, 51.69429153380586].

The regional bundle has six districts, 38 neighbourhoods and seven BAG places: Drimmelen, Hooge Zwaluwe, Lage Zwaluwe, Made, Terheijden, Wagenberg and Zevenbergschen Hoek. BRT supplies fifteen labels across two buurtschappen, three deelkernen, two gehuchten and eight woonkernen.
Five logical border links use A59 toward Oosterhout, A16/A59/N285 toward Moerdijk and N285 toward Breda. GM1719 has no ProRail station and has 42 GTFS stop areas.

CBS boundary OGC is half-yearly/CC BY 4.0; BAG is daily/Public Domain Mark; BRT is CC BY 4.0; NWB OGC/download is monthly/CC0 1.0; ProRail reference geometry is manually refreshed/CC0 1.0. OVapi GTFS is best effort/free-use with no SLA. These are reference geometry and schedules, not incident-time passability, capacity or utility topology.

evidenceSources.title: Omgevingsvisie climate/water theme, crisis preparedness and Rietlanden outer-dike project information
evidenceSources.edition: Omgevingsvisie adopted 18 November 2021; municipal pages current at access
supports: The adopted vision describes Drimmelen as flood-sensitive because of its water/Amer setting and says primary defences keep the area dry against high river and sea water; preserving their function is a leading principle. It assigns rain, groundwater and wastewater duties across the municipality, Brabantse Delta and Brabant Water.

The municipality identifies the greatest heat effects in parts of Made, the greenhouse area near Made and Terheijden. This is spatial planning context, not an incident footprint, temperature observation or T+72 forecast.

The Rietlanden page at https://drimmelen.nl/projecten-en-beleid/project-rietlanden-drimmelen, updated 16 July 2026, places the proposed harbour development outside the primary defence and discusses future ground/floor levels and warning measures; the plan is under appeal and does not establish current occupancy or failure.

The current crisis page at https://drimmelen.nl/ramp-crisis warns that extreme weather can disrupt power, telephone, shops and drinking water, includes cyber/major-disruption guidance and advises residents to be self-sufficient for three days. Guidance is not stock, activation, reachability, capacity or restoration evidence.
These HTML sources are operationally accessible but expose no stable feature API, open-data licence or fixed update cadence. Their safe simulation role is governance and hazard-mechanism context.

evidenceSources.title: Moerdijk-Drimmelen and Standhazensedijk defence projects, legal waterworks services and IMWA/DAMO registers
evidenceSources.edition: Preferred decision November 2025; public register snapshot 2 September 2026
supports: The Moerdijk-Drimmelen project covers about 17 kilometres of primary defence, is in planning for 2024-2031 and targets execution from 2028. Project material says sections do not meet current statutory norms but also says the dike is safe enough now; neither statement is live failure or guaranteed-protection evidence.

The 750-metre Standhazensedijk section was strengthened with a heave screen in 2024 and the project was reported complete in 2025: https://www.brabantsedelta.nl/projecten-in-jouw-buurt/dijkversterking-standhazensedijk/. Completion remains context, not incident-time condition.

The official ArcGIS MapServer at https://geoservices.brabantsedelta.nl/arcgis/rest/services/EXTERN/WEB_Vastgestelde_Legger_PrimaireKeringen/MapServer supports map/query/data plus WMS/WFS in EPSG:28992 for primary defences, protection zones, pumps, sluices, culverts and wastewater assets. The REST metadata states no standard licence or fixed cadence; legal geometry does not prove state or hydraulic connectivity.

The generated municipal intersection contains 164 public water objects: seven sewer pumps, two sluices, nineteen surface-water pumps, one RWZI and 135 weirs. Named registers include sewer pumps for Drimmelen, Terheijden, Made, Hollandsch Diep, Lage/Hooge Zwaluwe and Wagenberg and RWZI Lage Zwaluwe, but source capacities lack an app-wide unit/compatibility contract.

HWH IMWA is weekly and DAMO contributor-dependent via national OGC APIs under CC BY-SA 4.0. Coverage is partial; registered objects are suitable for context/completeness checks, never as proof of connectivity, operation, backup, capacity or restoration.

evidenceSources.title: Regionaal Risicoprofiel 2023-2027
supports: The profile evaluates extreme rain, drought, cold/snow/ice, heatwave, storm, flooding, nature fire, earthquake and digital/vital-infrastructure disruption. It classifies flooding as catastrophic, extreme weather and digital vital disruption as very serious, nature fire as serious and earthquake as considerable at regional level.
The profile names the Biesbosch among the region's largest nature areas and explains that heat/drought can raise ignition/spread risk while limited extinguishing-water access complicates response.

For the Benedenrivieren area it distinguishes sea, high-river, polder/defence-failure and extreme-weather flooding and explains that water levels can combine river discharge, sea storm surge and closure strategy. Outer-dike areas and primary defences require scenario-specific treatment.

It records cascade dependencies across power, gas, drinking water, telecom, roads, rail, navigation and 112. These are qualitative regional mechanisms, not Drimmelen neighbourhood probabilities, live service state or precise T+72 losses.

The fixed planning PDF has no machine event API, explicit open-data licence or live cadence. It should inform scenario selection, dependency hypotheses and operator exercises, not numeric calibration by itself.

evidenceSources.publisher: Gemeente Breda / Water- en Klimaatkring De Baronie
evidenceSources.title: Klimaatportaal ArcGIS services for water nuisance, flooding, heat and drought
evidenceSources.edition: Wateroverlast v5, overstromingen v4, hitte v3 and droogte v2 at access
supports: The public ArcGIS REST folders provide MapServer query/data output in EPSG:28992 for rain water depth/building impact/road passability, flooding, heat and drought. The rain service describes a 3Di exercise including 70 mm in one hour and a 0.25 m result cell, although layer naming and embedded descriptions also reference other design storms; edition semantics must be preserved rather than silently normalized.

The published service extents reach only Drimmelen's southern fringe around Terheijden and do not cover the full Amer/Biesbosch municipality. NoData outside that footprint must remain outside-coverage/Unknown, never zero exposure.

REST metadata does not provide a standard reuse licence, contractual refresh cadence or complete provenance/NoData contract for every layer. Those conditions require publisher confirmation before causal ingestion.

The safest current role is official partial-coverage planning/context and validation of qualitative rank patterns. It is not current rain, live road passability, a municipality-wide hazard surface or a T+72 forecast.

evidenceSources.title: Official combustible-nature, weather, seismic, flood, water-level and agricultural context services
evidenceSources.edition: Current service/catalogue editions at access; Risicokaart feature valid since 21 June 2006
supports: The official Risicokaart WFS returns Drimmelen feature isor_brandbaar_natuurgebied.1719200547312, Rupsenhoek / Sluishoek, classified loofbos and source-held by GM1719. Representative point [4.812900737065559, 51.7457033044792] lies inside that polygon and BU17190101 Verspreide huizen Biesbosch.

The WFS supports machine-readable JSON/GML/CSV/Shapefile, but GetCapabilities states no explicit reuse licence or fixed publication cadence. A 2006-validity register polygon is fuel/response context, not current fuel moisture, ignition, perimeter or suppression state.

KNMI Data Platform/FDSN provides versioned radar/weather and seismic observations; named radar products are generally five-minute observations under CC BY 4.0. Observation/issue/valid time and station/radar coverage must persist, and current observations cannot be relabeled as a T+72 forecast.

Rijkswaterstaat's PDOK flood-risk OGC API is CC0 and based on second-cycle reporting (2016-2021), with no planned refresh; it is coarse screening only. LIWO/LVO offers authority-selected, versioned flood scenarios for professional crisis management, but access/reuse terms and scenario provenance require explicit confirmation before integration.

Waterinfo generally provides ten-minute point observations under CC0 and is non-mission-critical. Zero Waterinfo points assigned inside GM1719 at the deployment snapshot is no local point coverage, not zero water level/discharge or safety. RVO's annual definitive BRP crop parcels are CC0 land-use context, not current fuel, yield or food stock.

evidenceSources.publisher: Netbeheer Nederland / Stichting Mijn Aansluiting / RIVM / DUO / RDI / NDW
evidenceSources.title: Machine-readable power-planning, provider, care, education, antenna and traffic public context
evidenceSources.edition: Provider and deployment snapshots inspected 2 September 2026; RIVM acute-care questionnaire 2026 v1.1
supports: A WFS point query at the municipal reference point identifies Enexis for electricity/gas, Brabant Water for drinking water and overlapping KPN/Ziggo/DELTA media responsibility. Mijn Aansluiting publishes these responsibility polygons with Public Domain Mark metadata; provider timestamps are present, but geometry is not cable/pipe topology, coverage quality, state or capacity.

One public postcode sample at 4927BB identifies Netbeheer Nederland's GT Geertruidenberg planning area: withdrawal 134.9 MW existing, 84.3 MW required and 58.4 MW queued across 118 requests; injection 127.7/89.1/86.1 MW across 87 requests, with TenneT congestion class 3 and nineteen projects. Capacity/projects refresh at least quarterly and queues monthly; the publisher calls the data open, but exact licence and endpoint stability are unstated. One sample is not municipal coverage, topology, outage, load or T+72 state.

The CC0 RIVM acute-care questionnaire v1.1, published 3 July 2026, has no acute-care point inside GM1719. Amphia Breda is an external regional-care context; absence inside the municipality is not absence of care access, and the register does not provide occupancy, staffing, diversion, generators, fuel or route state.

The generated context has fifteen DUO education locations (national daily refresh around 06:15 under attribution terms), 58 RDI antenna sites (live statutory WFS; reuse licence/cadence unstated), six coarse government points, zero current NDW situations and zero RIVM PM2.5 stations. Schools/offices are not shelters, antennas are not coverage/backhaul, and every zero is a coverage/time result rather than open/clean/safe state.

NDW's current DATEX snapshot is CC0 with publication time 2 September 2026 15:25Z and record-specific validity filtering. It can constrain current road-event context only; it cannot be projected as T+72 passability without forecast/scenario logic.

identity.summary: GM1719, Drimmelen, Noord-Brabant and safety region Midden- en West-Brabant are internally and officially coherent.
notes: Generated feature id, municipality code/name, province and exactly one safety-region assignment agree.
The context gate verifies centre [4.749560515173187, 51.69429153380586] lies inside the generated overview.
Boundary/statistics edition 2025, older planning/stress-test editions, current observations and synthetic exercise time remain distinct.

geography.summary: The one-component outline is topologically coherent, but its 87-position overview is too coarse for Amer, defence, outer-dike, road, woodland or facility intersection.
notes: Fresh official geometry has one component/one ring/1,178 positions; the overview preserves topology with only 87 positions.
Use the full-resolution annual CBS geometry and explicit land/water/coverage masks for analysis; retain the compact outline for overview selection/rendering only.
Representative neighbourhood points cannot stand in for complete hazard, resident, road, facility or asset geometry.

demography.summary: Official municipality controls and neighbourhood totals reconcile within CBS publication semantics.
notes: CBS and the 38 neighbourhood source rows both total 28,295 residents.
CBS reports 12,445 households and 6,873 residents aged 65+; neighbourhood rows sum to 12,440 and 6,870 respectively.
Largest population rows include Stuivezand 2,230, Vierendelen 2,005, Molenpolder 1,755, Hondenhei 1,670 and De Meede 1,585.
Registered residents are denominators, not timestamped presence, evacuation demand, visitor counts, care need or individual vulnerability.

regionalDetail.summary: Thirty-eight neighbourhoods give granular census context, but missing indicators and public registers cannot supply live hazard exposure or service state.
notes: District-heating and charging fields are missing for all 38 rows; property/housing/tenure/benefit fields are missing for three and cars-per-household for five.
Null and suppressed values remain Unknown, never zero. Coverage, effective/observation time, unit, quality and intended simulation role must survive ingestion/export.
The 164 water objects, fifteen education locations, 58 antenna sites and six government points are non-live context, not connectivity, occupancy, availability or restoration.

settlements.summary: BAG and BRT references retain seven principal places and rural labels without changing municipal identity.
notes: BAG places are Drimmelen, Hooge Zwaluwe, Lage Zwaluwe, Made, Terheijden, Wagenberg and Zevenbergschen Hoek.
BRT adds Binnen-Moerdijk, Blauwe Sluis, Drie Hoefijzers, Gaete, Helkant, Het Zand, Oud-Drimmelen, Steelhoven and Stuivezand, for fifteen generated settlement labels.
Settlement type/labels are cartographic context, not incident-time population, isolation, service continuity or hazard footprint.

transport.summary: Road and transit references are present, but the causal graph is five border-road proxies duplicated across all eight services.
notes: Five A16/A59/N285 links cover Breda, Moerdijk and Oosterhout with nominal scenario-unit capacities 260/150; these are not measured throughput, emergency access or future passability.
There is no ProRail station in GM1719; 42 GTFS stop areas are static reference/schedule context, not live bus, evacuation, ambulance or repair continuity.
All eight services expose identical road IDs. NWB cannot substantiate electricity, drinking-water, drainage, gas, telecom, facility or supply transfer.
Current NDW no-match is a time/coverage result. The partial De Baronie road-water layers do not cover all of GM1719.

emergencyContext.summary: Strong municipal, water-authority and safety-region context exists, but it is neither an incident-valid operational state nor a quantitative first-72-hour calibration.
notes: Evidence covers rain/river/sea interaction, primary and outer-dike areas, heat/drought, nature fire, storm/winter, earthquake screening, cyber and lifeline cascades.
Municipal three-day preparedness guidance does not prove stock, shelter, command-post, distribution or responder capacity.
No registered acute-care point lies inside GM1719; external Amphia context requires route/access modeling and does not prove acceptance or availability.
Current/no-match NDW, Waterinfo, PM2.5, power or seismic data must retain retrieval/valid time and cannot be projected into synthetic T+72.

scenarioMatrix.summary: All ten canonical presets execute at all six mandatory checkpoints for all eight services.
notes: MUNICIPALITY_AUDIT_CODE=GM1719 pnpm audit:model passed one file/two tests in 32.22 seconds (32.02 seconds test time) for severe-storm, pluvial-flood, river-flood, coastal-flood, heatwave, winter-storm, cyberattack, earthquake, wildfire and compound at T+0/6/12/24/48/72 across every service.
The apps/web/src/scenarios.ts factory delegates to sim-core, preventing a separate web preset implementation.

A focused reproduction with an official woodland-contained fire source passed one test in 33.10 seconds (33.01 seconds import; 1 ms test) and recorded scenario, spatial, network, ledger and recovery values.

A headless Chromium run at 1440x900 and 390x844 selected Drimmelen, river flood, Drinking water and T+24/T+72 with no console errors or horizontal overflow. The inspector showed 64% at both times, labeled the network a logical corridor proxy and correctly treated zero local Waterinfo observations as no data rather than zero/safe.

numericalInvariants.summary: Outputs are finite, bounded, deterministic, exact at zero input and locally reconciled.
notes: Exact-zero intensity gives zero maximum severity, affected population-equivalent and attributable person-hours for every preset.
Compound T+24 has 38 rows summing to population 28,295 and affected 16,534; maximum all-service reconciliation error is 3.552713678800501e-15.
Changing the selected service layer does not mutate municipality hazard, pressure or affected values.

spatialPlausibility.summary: One source-insensitive neighbourhood seed creates precise local ranks across unrelated hazards and contradicts official heat and woodland context.
notes: Pluvial, river, coastal, heat and wildfire have the exact same complete 38-neighbourhood order: Grienden, Verspreide huizen Biesbosch, Nieuwland, Stuivezand, Kleine Schans and Molenpolder lead each; Terheijden centrum ranks 37th.
The municipality identifies heat effects in Made and Terheijden, while official rain and woodland sources have distinct mechanisms and coverage. None determines the generated ordering.

With source [4.812900737065559, 51.7457033044792] inside the official Rupsenhoek/Sluishoek loofbos polygon and BU17190101 Verspreide huizen Biesbosch, direct fire peaks 0.372226 at T+12, yet Grienden leads and the containing neighbourhood ranks second.
The compound result declares no unsupported spatial hazard families even though none of the nine physical/cyber hazard families has a GM1719 local calibration contract.

serviceDependencies.summary: Every lifeline copies five NWB road links despite sector-specific public context and absent physical network evidence.
notes: The same five A16/A59/N285 link IDs and scenario-unit capacities are assigned to power, water, drainage, gas, telecom, mobility, facilities and supply.
The public 164-object water register, provider-responsibility polygons and grid-planning sample do not prove connectivity, flow, switching, current load, backup, outage or repair.

At river T+24 and T+72, power/water/drainage/gas/telecom/mobility/supply availability is exactly 0.810877/0.643640/0.445872/0.863609/0.665558/0.583877/0.645063. Facilities changes from 0.917318 to 0.684280 while every explicit recovery factor is zero.

Physical utility topology is unavailable or security-sensitive. The smallest safe fallback is a non-spatial, explicitly synthetic municipality service index with uncertainty—not invented road-network topology.

causalTrace.summary: Attribution ledgers close and distinguish matched no-event counterfactuals, but their precision exceeds the local empirical support.
notes: Hazard, local service, incoming-network and downstream cascade ledgers reconcile to their totals, and attributable burden is non-negative and cumulative.
The trace describes a matched no-event counterfactual and labels NWB flows as logical corridor proxies.
Attribution closure verifies internal arithmetic only. It does not validate generic neighbourhood ranks, defence/river behavior, route capacity, provider topology or restoration timing.
Official current observations, planning layers and registers are not used as simulated future state; the inspector must keep that distinction visible wherever a precise scenario percentage is shown.

recovery72h.summary: Standing-water persistence is numerically guarded, but river and compound first-72-hour trajectories lack an authority-backed event and restoration basis.
notes: River severity and normalized inundation stress remain 0.667903 and 2.145597 at T+24 and T+72; affected population-equivalent rises from 5,913 to 7,214 and attributable burden from 231,767.633 to 896,140.193 person-hours.

At both river checkpoints every explicit service recovery factor is zero. Six availability values remain bit-identical while facilities deteriorates despite no authority/provider restoration schedule.

Compound retains flood stress 0.248061 and power availability 0.153936 at T+24 and T+72; facilities falls from 0.736700 to 0.505377, all recovery factors remain zero, and burden reaches 879,142.511 person-hours.

The model needs selected water-boundary/defence/breach assumptions, connected footprints, arrival/recession and documented restoration priors. Otherwise T+0-72 values must be labeled synthetic exercise outputs with broad uncertainty.

findings.summary: The complete 10-preset by 6-checkpoint by 8-service execution, zero-input, deterministic, bounded, reconciliation, causal-ledger and layer-invariance contract passes.
findings.evidence: The mandatory focused gate passes two tests; the independent focused run passes. Compound T+24 reconciles all 38 rows and 28,295 people with maximum service error 3.552713678800501e-15, and all zero-intensity runs remain exactly zero.
findings.action: Keep GM1719 in the national regression matrix and retain exact-zero, sustained-water, local-sum, deterministic and causal-closure assertions when correcting evidence and spatial behavior.

findings.summary: The overview preserves topology but removes most official boundary vertices and cannot support local intersections.
findings.evidence: The official 2025 geometry has 1,178 positions; the generated overview has 87. The municipality spans Amer/Biesbosch water, primary/outer-dike settings and only partially covered climate layers, where boundary detail and coverage masks matter.
findings.action: Use the non-generalized PDOK/CBS 2025 geometry for analytics and explicit coverage masks; keep the 87-position outline for overview rendering only. Refresh half-yearly under CC BY 4.0 and preserve effective dates.

findings.summary: Generic river persistence is presented with false local precision without an Amer/Benedenrivieren boundary, defence or inundation scenario.
findings.evidence: Official local/regional evidence distinguishes primary and outer-dike areas and combined river-discharge, sea-surge and closure conditions. The model instead holds normalized inundation stress at 2.145597 through T+72, grows affected population-equivalent to 7,214 and burden to 896,140.193 person-hours, with no selected boundary, failure/non-failure case, connected depth/arrival/recession footprint or uncertainty. Coastal-flood direct depth is zero in the canonical run, which only means that preset's narrow synthetic direct component is zero—not no coastal/Benedenrivieren interaction.
findings.action: Before release, mark GM1719 river/coastal local amplitudes unsupported and expose affected/depth as Unknown unless the user selects a versioned LIWO/LVO or authority-approved scenario with boundary conditions, defence/breach state, connected footprint, arrival/recession and uncertainty. Keep Brabantse Delta legal/project layers as context, not live state.

findings.summary: A common synthetic seed gives five unrelated hazards the exact same 38-neighbourhood rank while declaring no unsupported family.
findings.evidence: Pluvial, river, coastal, heat and wildfire rank all neighbourhoods identically, led by Grienden and Verspreide huizen Biesbosch, with Terheijden centrum 37th. Municipal evidence instead highlights heat in parts of Made and Terheijden, and rain/flood/fire layers have different physical drivers. The compound output has unsupported: [] despite no GM1719 calibration contract.
findings.action: Replace the shared hash rank with hazard-specific official surfaces and geometry-weighted exposure. Until complete, emit Unsupported/Unknown per hazard family, source/edition/coverage/NoData fields and coarse uncertainty; never convert outside-coverage to low exposure.

findings.summary: The pluvial output ignores available hydraulic planning layers and their partial-coverage/edition semantics.
findings.evidence: The model reports T+24 flood stress 0.239648, 8,910 affected people-equivalent and mobility availability 0.321627 from generic inputs. De Baronie ArcGIS exposes queryable 3Di water-depth, building and road-passability layers but reaches only the southern fringe, has inconsistent event descriptions and lacks a complete licence/cadence/NoData contract. The municipality also assigns rain/groundwater/wastewater duties but publishes no live incident state.
findings.action: Negotiate/retrieve a municipality-wide, versioned hydraulic surface with explicit rain event, grid, vertical datum, validation, licence and NoData mask. Use the existing ArcGIS endpoints only as partial official context until those gates pass; combine observations/forecasts only with retained issue and valid times.

findings.summary: The wildfire footprint is not anchored to the official Rupsenhoek/Sluishoek woodland or Biesbosch response conditions.
findings.evidence: A controlled source inside Risicokaart feature isor_brandbaar_natuurgebied.1719200547312 and BU17190101 peaks direct fire at 0.372226 at T+12, yet Grienden ranks first and the containing neighbourhood second. The canonical preset is remote smoke-only, so it does not validate a local ignition. VRMWB identifies Biesbosch nature-fire exposure and limited extinguishing-water access as relevant mechanisms.
findings.action: Ingest the official WFS woodland geometry as context after licence/cadence confirmation, require a selected ignition/perimeter, and combine it with timestamped KNMI wind/dryness/fuel and response assumptions. If ignition/perimeter is absent, show local flame exposure Unknown; do not infer current fuel or suppression from a long-validity polygon.

findings.summary: Precise drinking-water and drainage availability is unsupported by connectivity, operating state or capacity evidence.
findings.evidence: The public intersection has 164 water objects, including seven sewer pumps, nineteen surface-water pumps, two sluices and RWZI Lage Zwaluwe. The model does not use their catchments, connectivity, controls, compatible capacity units, state, backup or repair. The browser displays drinking-water availability as exactly 64% at both river T+24 and T+72 although no local Waterinfo point or operational Brabant Water state is assigned.
findings.action: Integrate HWH IMWA/DAMO weekly/contributor-dependent CC BY-SA 4.0 and Brabantse Delta ArcGIS as non-live context first. Obtain authorized aggregate catchments, dependencies, unit contracts, live/state feeds and restoration priors before causal use; otherwise display Unknown or a clearly non-spatial synthetic service index.

findings.summary: All eight services are represented by the same five road links, which is not a physical lifeline topology.
findings.evidence: Power, water, drainage, gas, telecom, mobility, facilities and supply each expose identical A16/A59/N285 route IDs and nominal 260/150 scenario-unit capacities. Mijn Aansluiting provider polygons and one GT Geertruidenberg planning sample identify responsibility/congestion context only; neither supplies connectivity, current load, switching, redundancy, coverage, outage or restoration.
findings.action: Restrict NWB monthly CC0 geometry to mobility/reference use. Seek authorized sector-specific aggregate graphs and state feeds from providers/operators. Where unavailable or security-sensitive, use explicitly synthetic non-spatial indices with uncertainty and prevent route/capacity UI from implying physical topology.

findings.summary: Facilities, mobility and supply outputs lack local destinations, access, occupancy, backup and action-state evidence.
findings.evidence: GM1719 has no ProRail station, 42 GTFS stop areas, no internal RIVM acute-care point, fifteen education locations and six government points. The simulation does not model reachability to external acute care such as Amphia, verified reception/distribution sites, bus/road status, staffed capacity, generators/fuel, ambulance routing or resupply actions. Schools and offices are not shelters, and a station/register point is not live service.
findings.action: Use GTFS/NWB/NDW with explicit schedule/publication/valid time for mobility context; integrate RIVM v1.1 CC0 and confirmed municipal/VRMWB facility roles as destinations only. Require operator/municipal activation, access, occupancy and backup state for availability; otherwise keep those fields Unknown and add auditable interventions.

findings.summary: Storm, heat, winter, cyber and earthquake run coherently but remain uncalibrated synthetic exercises.
findings.evidence: At T+24 the severe-storm run gives severity 0.101321, pluvial/flood stress 0.182940 and power availability 0.644591; winter gives gust 16.310776 m/s, -5.105358 C, snow 2.072514 and mobility 0.216029; cyber gives cyber stress 0.436268 and telecom 0.479403. Heat retains 24.073075 C and drought stress 0.513952 at T+24 with water 0.376460. Earthquake peaks at T+2.25 with severity 0.005359/PGA 0.001715 g and zero affected at required checkpoints. VRMWB supports the hazard/cascade mechanisms but not these local numbers.
findings.action: Label every value synthetic scenario output, attach parameter provenance/uncertainty and use issue/valid-time-aware KNMI or authorized cyber/operator feeds only for explicit observed/forecast runs. Current observations cannot become T+72 forecasts; regional risk ratings cannot become neighbourhood probabilities.

findings.summary: River and compound T+24-72 continuity has no authority-backed restoration or action basis.
findings.evidence: River water/drainage remain exactly 0.643640/0.445872 at T+24 and T+72 and facilities worsens 0.917318 to 0.684280 while all recovery factors are zero. Compound power stays 0.153936 and facilities worsens 0.736700 to 0.505377, with 17,825 affected and 879,142.511 person-hours by T+72. Municipal three-day advice and public planning registers do not calibrate those trajectories.
findings.action: Add provider/authority restoration priors with provenance, uncertainty and explicit repair/resupply/evacuation actions; expose baseline, no-action and intervention runs separately. Without evidence, state that recovery is a synthetic exercise assumption rather than an operational forecast.

findings.summary: Public feeds have material spatial, temporal and semantic gaps that must remain Unknown.
findings.evidence: The deployment snapshot has zero local Waterinfo stations, zero RIVM PM2.5 points and zero current NDW situations; no internal acute-care point; complete missing charging/district-heat census fields; and partial southern climate-layer coverage. The inspector correctly calls Waterinfo a coverage gap, while precise scenario service percentages remain synthetic.
findings.action: Carry observed/issue/valid/retrieval time, edition, licence, geometry mask, unit, quality and NoData reason through ingestion and UI. Never map no match, outside coverage, suppression, stale data or unavailable topology to zero, normal, open or safe.

corrections.summary: Gate unsupported GM1719 hazard amplitudes and evidence state before exposing precise local impact.
corrections.validation: Add GM1719 to the audited unsupported-spatial registry for river, coastal, pluvial, heat, wildfire, storm, winter, earthquake and cyber until a documented local contract exists. Tests must require Unsupported/Unknown rather than a precise affected/depth claim, preserve exact-zero behavior, and show official context, observed/forecast and simulated evidence as separate states.

corrections.summary: Implement an authority-selected Amer/Benedenrivieren flood scenario with defence and valid-time provenance.
corrections.validation: Use full-resolution GM1719 geometry with a versioned LIWO/LVO or equivalent authority-approved raster/vector event: retain source, scenario id, boundary/closure conditions, defence/breach/non-breach state, vertical datum, cell size, issue/effective time, licence, coverage and NoData. Verify connected depths, outer-/inner-dike classification, arrival/recession and T+0-72 conservation; Brabantse Delta project/legal layers must remain non-live context.

corrections.summary: Replace common neighbourhood ranks with hazard-specific pluvial, heat and wildfire surfaces.
corrections.validation: For rain/heat, require a municipality-wide official surface or show partial-coverage/Unknown outside De Baronie's footprint; preserve event definition, grid, edition, licence and NoData. For fire, query the official Risicokaart WFS after licence/cadence clearance and require selected ignition/perimeter plus timestamped wind/fuel assumptions. Re-run the controlled Rupsenhoek/Sluishoek point and assert the containing footprint influences local rank.

corrections.summary: Separate managed-water registers and provider/planning areas from causal service topology and state.
corrections.validation: Ingest HWH weekly IMWA/contributor-dependent DAMO CC BY-SA 4.0, Brabantse Delta legal ArcGIS, Mijn Aansluiting Public Domain responsibility polygons and NBNL quarterly/monthly planning data as context only. Causal use must require unit-normalized capacity, connected catchments/topology, operational state, backup and restoration provenance. If unavailable/security-sensitive, assert a non-spatial explicitly synthetic fallback with uncertainty and no fake road topology.

corrections.summary: Add evidence-valid mobility, external-care, facility and T+72 continuity semantics.
corrections.validation: Keep NWB monthly CC0, GTFS schedule and NDW CC0 valid-time records distinct; route to confirmed external acute-care and activated municipal destinations without treating schools/offices as shelters. Require access, staffing/occupancy, backup and operator restoration evidence for facility availability. Tests must reject current observations as T+72 forecasts and no-match/no-point/outside-coverage as zero or safe.

residualLimitations: Electricity, gas, drinking-water, sewer, telecom and facility physical topology, live state, switching/control logic, backup, crew/fuel stock and restoration are unavailable or security-sensitive; public provider geometry and asset registers cannot fill those gaps.
No authority-selected Amer/Benedenrivieren flood boundary, defence/breach state, connected depth/arrival/recession footprint or live water-level station is assigned to the canonical scenario.
The De Baronie climate services cover only the southern fringe and lack a complete licence/cadence/NoData contract; municipality-wide hydraulic and heat calibration remains unavailable.

Risicokaart combustible-nature geometry is long-validity context, not current fuel moisture, ignition, perimeter or suppression. KNMI/RWS observations are not forecasts beyond their explicit valid times.

CBS registered population, BAG/BRT places, schools, government points, antennas, provider areas, stations/stops and crop parcels do not give incident-time people, occupancy, service, accessibility, stock or coverage quality.
Exact local percentages, ranks and person-hours are synthetic exercise outputs until each hazard/service has a versioned calibration, uncertainty and evidence-state contract.

Noord-Brabant review: establish municipality-wide rain/heat coverage and resolve De Baronie ArcGIS licence, event-description inconsistency, edition, cell-size and NoData semantics before causal use.
Noord-Brabant review: validate Risicokaart Rupsenhoek/Sluishoek and Biesbosch nature-fire coverage, publisher cadence/licence and ignition/fuel/wind/response inputs with VRMWB and land managers.

Noord-Brabant review: seek authorized aggregate water, power, telecom, care and continuity dependencies; retain public registers/provider areas as context and use transparent non-spatial synthetic fallback wherever topology/state is unavailable or sensitive.
